Subject: Data residency + deletion: EU-specific ask

Hi Laura,

Quick intro — I'm Aria (Head of Ops at FinCorp). We're evaluating Redwood for a payments analytics product and EU data residency + retention controls are a gating factor for procurement. Our security team needs the following clarified before we proceed: 

- Per-tenant data residency (ability to pin a tenant's data to EU regions only)
- Configurable retention windows per tenant (90/180/365 days or custom) with automated purge
- Deletion evidence (audit logs + object-level deletion records)
- Migration/retroactive deletion for existing records if tenant flips region

I'm attaching a short requirements PDF and a spreadsheet that shows how we'd like settings surfaced in the console. Can you share an engineering-level plan and an estimated timeline (ETA for an MVP + production rollout)? We can be flexible on timing but need commitments for contractual language.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if easier.

Aria Singh

Team — forwarding an external ask from FinCorp (high-value prospect; deal FIN-2026-09). Security is asking for per-tenant residency + configurable retention + automated purge with deletion evidence. High-level asks are in the attached spreadsheet.

High-level product requirements I want us to scope for an initial proposal: 
- Tenant-level region pinning (UI + API) to constrain storage/compute to chosen region(s)
- Per-tenant retention policies (preset windows + arbitrary TTL) that produce automatic purges
- Delete/audit trail: immutable audit records AND exportable deletion receipts for customers
- Migration flow: safe retroactive deletion for historical data when a tenant changes residency
- Controls surfaced in Console + Admin API + RBAC filtering

Questions for engineering for the initial reply to FinCorp (please reply-all with answers by EOD Monday):
1) Rough implementation approach (control plane vs data plane changes) and high-level risks
2) Minimum viable scope we can ship in 8–12 weeks (T-shirt estimate S/M/L)
3) Storage/backing-store implications (S3 buckets per-region? per-tenant prefixes?)
4) Audit log architecture for deletion receipts (where/how long retained)
5) Any compliance blockers (KMS integrations, cross-region snapshots)

I've started a Drive folder (link below) with the requirements doc and asked CS to prep contract language. Attaching the spreadsheet here for their view.

Next steps I propose after your replies: 1) Reply to FinCorp with a single-sheet plan and recommended ETA; 2) Create INF-1423 with dev tasks; 3) Schedule RFC review + signoff.

Subject: Re: Data residency + deletion: EU-specific ask

Thanks for the clear ask, Laura. Quick initial engineering notes and open questions below. I've created a stub ticket INF-1423 and uploaded a draft dev-scope.attachment.

Proposed two-phase approach (to minimize risk):
Phase 1 — Residency selectors + metadata-only enforcement (6–8 wks):
- Add per-tenant metadata to pin region(s) at the control plane level
- Ensure routing layer prefers region-local infra for new writes
- Introduce per-tenant retention policy object (API + UI) but implement purge as a manual/cron job guarded by feature flag

Phase 2 — Automated purge + evidence (8–12 wks after Phase 1):
- Build retention engine that runs scheduled deletions per-tenant/namespace with strong idempotency and retry semantics
- Emit deletion receipts to an append-only audit store (WAL) and surface export endpoint for customers
- Integrate with KMS to ensure deleted data keys are handled appropriately

Key technical concerns / questions:
- Backing store: we recommend region-bucket-per-region. Per-tenant prefixes inside region buckets are simpler but complicate true deletion guarantees if cross-region snapshoting exists.
- Cross-region replication & snapshots: we need a plan to find/expire old snapshots; otherwise, deletions may be incomplete.
- Reprocessing/migrations: retroactive deletion of existing data will be expensive; we should consider a "shred+confirm" job and an SLA for completion window.
- Audit log retention: how long does FinCorp expect receipts kept? We need to balance cost vs compliance retention policies.

Deliverables I can commit to for an initial reply to FinCorp:
- Short one-pager with Phase 1/Phase 2 scope and rough ETA (will provide by Mon EOD)
- Create INF-1423 with initial break down of tasks + spike for snapshot discovery (by Mon)

I'll attach the dev-scope draft to the ticket. Questions for product: do we need to support per-object retention policies or is tenant-level sufficient for this RFP?

Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifications and next steps: 

- For FinCorp's procurement window we should propose Phase 1 as an "MVP" that delivers region pinning + policy objects + manual purge capability. Phase 2 will be sold as "Automated Purge + Deletion Receipts (GA)".
- Product answer: tenant-level retention + auto-purge is sufficient for the RFP; per-object TTL can be a follow-on.
- Audit retention ask from FinCorp: they want deletion receipts retained for 2 years (they'll confirm in writing).

Next steps (action owners):
- Karthik: deliver the one-pager and INF-1423 task breakdown by EOD Mon (owner: Karthik)
- Grace: coordinate with CS to draft contract language for Phase 1/Phase 2 (owner: Grace)
- Vivek: flag any infra capacity needs for region-buckets and snapshot discovery (owner: Vivek)
- Laura: I'll consolidate and reply to FinCorp with the plan + ETA; schedule RFC review for Wed 10am PT

I'll reply to FinCorp later today with the Phase 1 proposal and tentative ETA window (6–8 wks). Please assume a canary rollout and that CS/FinCorp will be in the first wave for validation.
